heading: Max-heap tracks k closest points
body:
Use a **max-heap of size k** storing negated distances. The root = **farthest** of the k closest so far.

When a new point is closer than the root → replace it.

**Trick:** Store `x² + y²` instead of `√(x² + y²)` — same ordering, no sqrt!

heading: Why max-heap, not min-heap?
body:
Min-heap gives you the **closest** point instantly, but you need the **farthest of the k closest** to decide if a new point qualifies.

Max-heap of size k: root = farthest of k → O(log k) to evict and insert.

label: Crux · Python

q: Why do we use a max-heap instead of a min-heap for this problem?
options: To keep track of the k farthest points and replace them with closer ones
To keep track of the k closest points and efficiently access the farthest of them
Because Python's heapq only supports max-heaps natively
To improve the time complexity to O(n)
explain: Max-heap of size k keeps the k closest points with the farthest at the root for O(log k) replacement.
